response_text: Co-operative multitasking is through the osYield function where the user chooses when the thread should be switched. This leads to an issue where if a thread yields or runs too long, the other threads may be starved. A solution to this is pre-emptive multitasking is controlled by the system through a system timer. The OS automatically interrupts threads based on a timer to ensure fairness. These points are from the user perspective where it may be easier for the OS to control multitasking. In the OS perspective, co-operative multitasking is easier where a context switch only needs to be performed when a thread explicitly yields. To add on, managing forced context switches is a difficult process especially when one thread is not ready to yield.\n
